title: Redis CLI Basics
description: Master redis-cli for connecting, inspecting data, running commands, scripting, and debugging production issues from the terminal.

data.text: The Redis command-line interface is a fast, scriptable way to inspect and manipulate data. Most production debugging starts in redis-cli before any application code changes.

Connect to a local or remote server with `redis-cli -h host -p port`. If authentication is enabled, pass `-a password` or use the interactive `AUTH` command. Use `PING` to verify connectivity instantly.

data.title: Common redis-cli connection patterns
data.content: Connect locally, authenticate, and test the connection.
data.code:
redis-cli ping
redis-cli -h 10.0.0.5 -p 6379 -a secret auth myuser
redis-cli --tls -h prod.redis.example.com ping

data.text: Use `KEYS` only in development. In production, prefer `SCAN` to iterate safely without blocking. Get key metadata with `OBJECT ENCODING` and `OBJECT REFCOUNT` to understand memory usage.

data.title: Safe key scanning in redis-cli
data.content: Iterate cache keys by pattern without blocking the server.
data.code:
redis-cli --scan --pattern 'user:*'
redis-cli scan 0 match 'session:*' count 100
redis-cli object encoding 'session:abc123'

data.text: Start an interactive session with `redis-cli`. You can run any Redis command without typing the prefix. Use `SELECT` to switch databases, `DBSIZE` to count keys, and `FLUSHDB` only when you mean to wipe everything.

data.title: FLUSHDB is irreversible
data.text: Never run FLUSHDB or FLUSHALL on production without a confirmed maintenance window and verified backup.

data.title: C# memory-check helper
data.content: Call redis-cli from C# to run INFO memory and parse the output when you need live metrics inside a .NET admin tool.

data.title: Essential monitoring commands
items: **INFO** — snapshot of server stats, memory, replication, and clients.
**SLOWLOG GET** — retrieve the slow query log to find expensive commands.
**MONITOR** — stream every command in real time; use only briefly for debugging.
**CLIENT LIST** — inspect connected clients, their IPs, and idle time.

data.caption: Redis CLI debugging workflow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Production issue] --> B[redis-cli -h host ping]
    B --> C{Alive?}
    C -->|No| D[Network / firewall check]
    C -->|Yes| E[INFO memory]
    E --> F{Near maxmemory?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Review eviction policy]
    F -->|No| H[SLOWLOG GET]
    H --> I[Identify slow commands]
    I --> J[Fix application code or config]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: redis-cli is indispensable for production debugging and scripting.
Always prefer SCAN over KEYS in production environments.
Use SLOWLOG and INFO to find memory and performance issues quickly.
